label: Counterfactual guidance by an outweighed reason: raising it alone would make it prevail
term: counterfactual guidance by an outweighed reason (GuidedByOutweighed)
definition: GuidedByOutweighed w good ctrl φ s r x y: the reason for y in respect r is outweighed at s (DEF 35ab5a34-4c6a-4327-97a2-a739a4263257), and in some scenario t that agrees with s on the control and raises y's weight in respect r alone (RaisesOnly: every other respect weighs every candidate as at s, respect r weighs every other candidate as at s, and weighs y more) the profile favours y over x. The reason itself makes the difference, not the removal of what outweighs it. It is a counterfactual, profile-level property, not registration of the reason in the source's actual state. Example: an agent who passes over the kinder plan only because the other is fairer, and takes it when its kindness alone is increased enough. Non-examples: a favouring fixed to x; a favouring blind to respect r (respectBlindNotGuided).
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#2145 premise lane C, round 3), attribution deferred. See docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'Counterfactual guidance and self-application against imitability exemplars'. An earlier draft required only some scenario keeping r's ranking in which the favouring follows y; the semantic challenge showed that a profile blind to r passed it (the flip came from removing the outweighing respect), so the definition now requires r alone to be raised. Registration of the outweighed reason in the actual state is a separate, realization-level question (degreeOnlyRegistersNoRespectBetweenTies).
